sentences.do_not_sum: Do not add Energy to Non-Energy, Goods, or Services. They are separate analytical aggregates. Goods includes total IPPI, so it is not a non-energy transmission measure and it is not added to the Energy sector.
sentences.headline_versus_ex_energy: Monthly IPPI excluding energy is +0.28% and scores production-network pressure as STABLE. Headline IPPI, which includes energy, is +1.962% month over month. IPPI energy and petroleum products are +12.084% month over month. Quarterly Energy sector PPI is +19.847% q/q in 2026-Q2, released 2026-10-09T08:30. Data age is 24 days after that release. That quarterly energy move is not added to the production-network channel. Headline IPPI and the Energy sector can move when IPPI excluding energy does not. The scored production-network channel uses only the monthly ex-energy index.
sentences.no_pass_through_model: No pass-through elasticity is estimated. These are separate observed price changes, not a structural Prima decomposition and not a reproduction of the Bank of Canada's model.
sentences.raw_materials: Monthly RMPI excluding crude energy is -0.435% and scores the stored imported_pressure channel as FALLING. This is StatCan's raw-materials price index for purchases by Canadian manufacturers, including domestically produced materials. It is not an import-price index. RMPI crude energy is +14.42% month over month and is not part of that channel. No import-price series is pinned, so imported cost pressure is not labeled.
sentences.revision: Each quarterly release can revise the previous two quarters. Weight updates revise the index back to the start of the new weight reference year. This feed stores the latest vintage only, not a real-time history. Observable release vintages in this response: 1. Back history published on the first public release (2026-10-09) was not observable in earlier quarters. A scored change is not proposed: the sample is not a real-time track record, the indexes are quarterly, and no Prima weights or elasticities are published.
sentences.score_guard: The quarterly sector layer is shadow-only. It is not in the direction, strength, or net vote, and it does not replace monthly IPPI excluding energy or RMPI excluding crude energy.
sentences.sensitivity: Quarterly q/q readings are not classified with the monthly IPPI or RMPI bands. The monthly bands are unchanged, and these quarterly changes are not in the scored vote. Proposed scored change: none.

method.note: Live authorities remain canonical. This artifact is a compact research snapshot. US, Australia, ECB FX, and CFTC positioning remain packet-level preflight. A stale Canadian benchmark yield stays visible on CA_rates and does not by itself mark the packet stale. CA-dependent expressions and existing-book positions that depend on that leg fail closed. Canadian benchmark freshness uses the Canadian business-day calendar and a one-session publication lag. NZ and Japan are not required_for_trader_preflight; a blocked RBNZ source or a Japan holiday-calendar print stays visible on that source and does not by itself mark the packet stale. NZ-dependent and JP-dependent expressions still fail closed. The official RBNZ B2 XLSX is tried first, including a browser-TLS retry, then the official RBNZ B2 HTML table. No vendor or media substitute is used. Japan JGB freshness uses the Tokyo business-day calendar and a one-session publication lag. Euro-area Bund (Germany) and Japan JGB cash curves remain six-economy rate legs. Cross-country spreads use exact common observation dates only. Policy-path context uses official overnight benchmarks plus public money-market data. The required tradable paper rates universe remains SOFR via CME SR3, CORRA via MX CRA, and AONIA via ASX IB. TONA is included when JPX OSE 3M settlements pass identity checks; FST3/€STR stays observe_only until a public settlement feed is reliable. Official government zero/forward curves are supplemental bond-curve inputs and are not required to manufacture a swap curve. Euro-area sovereign fragmentation (IT/FR/ES vs Bund) is market context, never an EA temperature input. Housing context is collected for the US, Canada and Australia from free maintained public sources: FHFA/Census/Fed/Freddie Mac via FRED for the US, Statistics Canada/CMHC/Bank of Canada for Canada, and ABS/RBA for Australia. EA/JP housing is omitted until an official/free source meets the contract. CFTC TFF supplies trader-class ownership/crowding context and can mark the packet stale. CME's public volume/open-interest service is a supplemental overlay and does not flip packet status. No historical warehouse is written to GitHub or Supabase.
